newsitem.title: JAPAN: Citibank to issue dual samurai - sources.
newsitem.headline: Citibank to issue dual samurai - sources.

text.p: Citibank, a unit of Citicorp, is expected to launch a dual-currency U.S. dollar/yen samurai bond on Thursday and become the first foreign commercial bank to issue such a bond, underwriting sources said on Wednesday.
They said the issue amount would be 20-30 billion yen with a prospective maturity of two to three years.
The lead manager is expected to be Daiwa Securities Co.
The Citibank samurai would be the first issue after the recent deregulation by the Ministry of Finance (MOF).
The MOF said on Monday it would allow foreign commercial banks to issue samurai bonds -- yen-denominated bonds issued in Japan by non-residents -- effective April 1.
Foreign commercial banks had been banned from issuing yen-denominated bonds here partly because of a regulation restricting the number of Japanese banks that can issue yen bonds at home.
Lifting this ban is part of government efforts to deregulate Japan's financial markets and is also in response to requests from foreign governments and banks, a ministry official said.
